problem: Native fixture evidence documented Word protection flags and real Excel macro sheets, but the index lacked permanent coverage of the DOC protection row and BIFF macro-sheet behavior, including publication boundaries and ordinary-sheet coexistence.
changes: Add four native DOC regressions for comments/forms protection, default refusal, explicit caller authorization, retained DOP/comment/FFData metadata, file publication and inverse authority.

Add two native regressions in each Excel owner for complete macro-tab catalogs, precise ordinary-worksheet API boundaries, real macro body/index evidence and ordinary-sheet edits that preserve the inert macro data.
Add two operations and two facade regressions for protected Word writes and macro-tab query/path/text behavior across eager and automatic source modes.
Index fourteen new tests, bringing the total to 342 tests and scoped partial assertions for 253 feature rows. No production code or fixture bytes changed.

verification_scope.doc_comments: Native Word2013 DOP has comments_or_read_only true, other protection flags false and key zero. The document has seven paragraphs and one Ryker Zhu/RZ comment with tag 435933812, reference CP 136, range [118,136), timestamp 2026-10-15 16:20 and exact PROTECTION_COMMENT_008 text. No range-protection table is present.
verification_scope.doc_forms: Native Word2013 forms protection has form_fields true, other protection flags false and key zero. The complete 694-byte DOP and three FFData models remain unchanged when an unrelated same-length title edit is explicitly authorized; unrelated CFB streams, including Data, are preserved.
verification_scope.doc_policy: Reads and exact no-ops succeed by default. Changed paragraph staging reports Body(Invalid(ProtectionDenied(Document))) and remains atomic. An explicit ProtectionAuthorization actor/reason allows the test edit without removing native protection. File reopen retains protection and comments; an inverse on the authorized package restores exact bytes, while a fresh destination without retained authority returns Body(Refused(Protected)). Public writes return DocumentProtected.
verification_scope.xls_catalog: Eager and source catalogs retain visible Macro_016 at complete index 0 and Sheet1 at complete index 1/worksheet ordinal 0. The native macro substream starts at 15466, contains 510 bytes and 38 records, has BOF type 0x0040 and three LabelSst cells (rows 0..2, column 0, indices 4..6). Those shared strings resolve to MACROSHEET_MARKER_016, INERT_LABEL_ONLY_016 and END_MACROSHEET_016. There are no Formula records.
verification_scope.xls_publication: Inserting ordinary worksheet text at D4 preserves the macro records, its shared-string values and valid INDEX pointers to DefColWidth/DBCell. The complete tab catalog and other CFB streams remain intact, file save/reopen reads the new text and inverse restores the complete original bytes.
verification_scope.xlsm: The macro workbook flavor, active macro tab and two-tab catalog remain visible. Cell, range and extent access to the macro tab return NotWorksheet. The 1407-byte macro XML hash matches the native audit. Ordinary D4 edit changes only sheet1.xml and documented recalculation properties in workbook.xml; every other workbook XML event and package member is retained. File save/reopen keeps macro flavor and the inverse restores all members.
verification_scope.xlsb: Eager and source catalogs agree on both tabs, active catalog position 0 and no active worksheet ordinal. The 490-byte macro part and 61-byte binary index match native hashes; index records are 0x002A/24 bytes, 0x0028/30 bytes and 0x0115/0 bytes. Macro materialization and indexed-value access return exact UnsupportedFeature errors despite the present index. Ordinary D4 edit changes only the ordinary sheet and its index, preserves every macro member, reads through the ordinary binary index after file reopen and inversely restores exact original bytes.
verification_scope.public_views: Both source modes query two sheet nodes and find Macro_016 with path round trips. Ordinary worksheet text/cells remain readable; non-grid macro content is intentionally outside that text projection and is separately proven present in owner tests. Explicit macro cell selection yields UnsupportedCapability for XLS and UnsupportedType for XLSM/XLSB. Facade ordinary-cell edits retain this catalog and boundary after reopen.
verification_scope.limits: No dialog sheet is present in these native specimens. Macro formulas and VBA payloads are absent; no code, macro, formula, entry/exit callback or external refresh executes. The protection fixtures have no password hash or protected-range bookmark evidence, and caller authorization is not authentication. No native Office reopen/rendering is claimed. XLSM inverse equality is package-member equality, not ZIP transport identity.
